abstract.p: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation, which predicts users' future destinations based on their potential interests, has emerged as a critical task in location-based social networks (LBSNs). However, this task remains challenged by issues such as popularity bias, exposure bias, and limited representational capacity, all of which impede the accurate modeling of users and POIs, thereby restricting balanced and effective recommendations. Therefore, we propose Trajectory Collaborative Filtering Mamba (TCFMamba), which integrates two specially designed modules, i.e., Joint Learning of Static and Dynamic Representations (JLSDR) and Preference State Mamba Network (PSMN), for debiased Point-of-Interest recommendation. Firstly, we design a location-aware and period-aware position encoder that fully utilizes the flexible modeling capacity of state-space models; Secondly, we effectively capture the temporal evolution of user preferences by leveraging trajectory collaborative filtering signals. Extensive experiments are conducted on three real-world datasets, and TCFMamba outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in POI recommendation tasks, achieving performance gains of 2.04% to 7.81%, while maintaining high levels of diversity and fairness. The results demonstrate that TCFMamba effectively mitigates semantic information dilution, addressing both popularity and exposure biases while enhancing the flexibility of preference state representation. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TCFMamba-0B10.
